Package threepl.exec

Class Queue

java.lang.Object
threepl.exec.Var
threepl.exec.ClockedVar
threepl.exec.Queue
All Implemented Interfaces:
TDEConstants, Constant
public final class Queue extends ClockedVar implements Constant, TDEConstants
This class represents a QUEUE mode variable. The variable has a name String, a mode and a Type, which may be complex. If the variable is a module, procedure or function parameter it may have an indirect pointer to another Var, depending on its mode and whether input or output. If the variable is a target mode it will also have an expanded name to ensure that this instance is unique. The current clock name String and TDEVar is also stored in this class.

There is an ArrayList of all assignments to this variable. Each assignment is entered into the list one bit at a time. Entries in this list are triples -

  • the bit number, which is an Integer
  • the source of the bit, which is a TDEVar
  • the select signal causing the assignment, which is a TDEVar
The following special cases apply -
  • If isInPar is true then this variable is a module, procedure or function input parameter.
  • If isOutPar is true then this variable is a module or procedure output parameter.
  • If iclk is not equal to pclk then the queue buffer is asynchronous (input and output have different clocks).

    • getRef

      public Ref getRef(VarNode varnode, SubFieldList sfl, boolean is_val, SrcLoc loc)
      Get a reference to a variable. The reference is generally used for assignment to a variable however the value of a variable can also obtained by starting with the reference. The main information contained in the reference is -
      • a list of words in the variable selected by subscripts or field names
      • a list of primitive types for each word
      • for target variables a list of bit pairs associated with the word list
      • a multi-dimensioned array giving the dimensionality of the reference
      • a type to make sure assignment types match
      • a TDEVar for a target variable
      The varnode argument is used to get any flags associated with the variable occurrence (++ or -- flags of the string indirect operator/flag), but it may be null if the reference is being requested in some other context. The subs argument is a list of subscript or field nodes associated with the variable occurrence - it may be null. A pointer variable returns a reference to the ultimate variable to which it points. A target reference includes a TDEVar signal for the reference.
      Overrides:
      getRef in class Var
      Parameters:
      varnode - is the tree node for the variable occurrence or is null if the reference is not associated with a variable occurrence (used to detect ++, -- or ?)
      sfl - is the list of associated subscript and field nodes after the subscript and field nodes have been evaluated
      is_val - indicates that we want a value rather than a reference
      loc - is the source file location
      Returns:
      the reference to the variable

    • addPop

      public void addPop(Scope module_scope, TDEVar tdev, SrcLoc loc)
      Register a pop of this queue variable by a destination module. The pop signal structure is a HashMap to which the Module is the key. The value is a HashSet containing one or more execution TDEVars. Thus for a queue variable we have a map containing one or more modules. For each module we have a set of one or more execution signals. Note that redundant calls to this method for the same execution signal in the same module do no harm as they will map to the same single entry. will be treated as if from within a single module.
      Parameters:
      module_scope - is the scope of the Module we are in
      tdev - is the pop signal
      loc - is the source file location
